title: Territorial routing, escalation & data-retention notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working note that centralizes operator guidance, escalation paths, and retention constraints for territorial routing and region-pin enforcement across Private deployments. The goal: reduce ambiguity when requests land with ambiguous geography or when an enforcement decision could impact SLA or customer data residency commitments. This is intentionally operational and partial — use it alongside the canonical residency policy (Confluence: CONFLUENCE-RESD-47).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Primary enforcement model: directory-level pin annotations + runtime routing policies.
- Fallback order for ambiguous locality: (1) customer pin -> (2) explicit request-region header -> (3) geo-IP -> (4) default-region for tenant.
- If enforcement would violate SLA (latency breach, capacity shortage), follow the escalation matrix below before making a routing fallback.
- Retention: operator telemetry kept 90d by default; audit evidence for residency decisions stored 2 years for enterprise contracts.

Common operational scenarios and guidance:

1) Request arrives with customer pin mismatch (request-region header says eu-west but tenant pin = us-east)
- If model instance for pinned region is available within 250ms route window: route to pinned region.
- If no capacity in pinned region: attempt canary fallback to equivalent pinned-model in other region only after approval (see Escalation matrix).
- Preserve evidence: log request headers, routing decision, capacity snapshot, and the operator ID if manual override applied.

2) Geo-IP indicates a country with strict sovereignty (e.g., DE/FR/BR/SG) but customer has not pinned region
- Default: treat as advisory. Notify customer via scheduled ticket (CS owns outbound comms).
- If customer signs a residency addendum or contract requires automatic enforcement, update tenant pin in the control plane and document via ticket.

3) Cross-border replay (historical request replay to a different region for debugging)
- Prohibited for customers with residency compliance flag set. For other customers: redact PII, get written owner consent, create a short-lived staging tenant with explicit region pin.

Decision matrix: when to fallback vs. delay
- Minor latency > target (up to +50ms): retry to pinned region with extended timeout.
- Latency breach > 300ms or 5% error spike: open incident, notify SRE, do not auto-fallback unless SRE authorizes.
- Capacity exhausted in pinned region and queued requests > 2min: escalate to capacity ops for burst allocation.

Escalation matrix (who to call, in order):
- On-call operator (first 15 minutes): triage, attempt soft remediation (recycle instance, clear queue of stalled jobs).
- Capacity-ops (15-45 minutes): apply reserved burst or reassign capacity.
- Eng-private-deployments lead (45-90 minutes): approve temporary cross-region fallback if required and log an exception.
- Legal & Security (immediate if customer contract flagged or possible PII exposure): consult before any cross-region fallback.

Checklist for manual override (operator must fill these in case of an exception):
- Reason for override (short text)
- Evidence attached (logs, capacity snapshot ids, ticket id)
- Approval: capacity-ops or eng lead (name + timestamp)
- TTL for override (max 24 hours, unless legal approves otherwise)

Telemetry & observability primitives to add to incidents:
- Per-request residency_decision enum (PINNED|HEADER|GEOIP|DEFAULT)
- routing_path trace id and region hop history (for audits)
- pre-enforcement latency and post-enforcement latency samples (5s/30s windows)
- capacity_snapshot tag with pool id and available_gpus
- incident_evidence_id used to attach artifacts to a billing/audit bundle

Retention policy notes (practical):
- Operator telemetry (logs, traces): 90 days default.
- Audit bundles for enterprise residency commitments: 730 days (2y). These bundles are generated for any manual override or when a request used a fallback path that would otherwise violate the explicit region pin.
- Low-sensitivity metrics and aggregated histograms: indefinite (per product analytics policy).

Example operator runbook snippets (pseudocode for enforcement middleware):
- "// simplified enforcement logic used at edge routing"
- "decision = if tenant.pin then PINNED else if req.header.region then HEADER else GEOIP;"
- "if decision == PINNED and pool.available(pinned_region) then route(pinned_region)"
- "else if decision == PINNED and not pool.available then"
- "  create_audit_bundle(); notify_capacity_ops();"
- "  if manual_override_granted then route(fallback_region) with tag OVERRIDE_{operator_id}"

Unresolved questions / open items (action owners assigned):
- Default TTL for pinless tenants in controlled countries (owner: Olivia) -> proposal due 2024-03-20.
- How to represent multi-party residency agreements (B2B reseller scenarios) in the control plane (owner: Diego) -> prototype spec required.
- Formal SLA delta to publish if cross-region fallback occurs (owner: Product-hosted-api) -> needs legal sign-off.

Sample evidence export fields (what to include in an audit bundle):
- request_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id, decision_reason, route_target, fallback_reason (if any), operator_override_id (if any), capacity_snapshot_id, trace_id, original_headers (redact authorization credentials), geoip_lookup_result, ticket_id linking to customer comms

Notes on automation safeguards (to reduce manual exceptions):
- Auto-burst only if an enterprise contract exists and auto-burst flag is true on tenant profile. Otherwise require capacity-ops approval.
- Rate-limit auto-fallbacks per tenant to 3 per 24h window. Exceeding requires human review.
- When doing auto-fallback due to capacity, annotate returned tokens with an internal metadata header (X-RW-RegionFallback: <region>) so downstream telemetry and audits can filter.

Communications template (operator -> CS ticket to inform customer of fallback)
- Subject: Residency routing fallback observed for tenant <tenant_id> on <date>
- Body (short): We observed requests from your project being routed from <pinned_region> to <fallback_region> because <reason>. No customer data was retained outside the fallback region beyond standard transient caches. We've opened ticket <ticket_id> for tracking and will provide audit bundle on request.

Appendix: quick region sensitivity table (non-exhaustive)
- EU (DE, FR): high (prefer automatic enforcement when possible).
- LATAM (BR): medium-high (data localization laws for certain sectors).
- APAC (SG): high for financial/health; variable for other sectors.
- US: low (federal law less prescriptive re: residency), but state laws + sector regs may apply.

Final notes and next steps:
- Action: add the residency_decision enum and routing_path hop logs to the runtime trace schema (owner: Samir; ETA: 2024-03-12).
- Action: implement audit bundle generator as a callable service with signed manifests (owner: Eng infra; ETA: 2024-04-01).
- Action: CS + Legal to finalize customer-facing fallback language (owner: Evelyn; ETA: 2024-03-25).

If you are executing an override: copy this doc link into the ticket and ensure the operator override checklist lines are filled before closing the incident.

End of note.

Revision history:
- 2024-02-12: initial draft (Maya)
- 2024-02-20: added retention clarifications and checklist (Diego)
- 2024-03-05: updated escalation timings and telemetry fields (Samir)
